//: Which files may be written in which phase. Read by .claude/hooks/guard-phase.mjs on Cursor's preToolUse and Claude Code's PreToolUse. Hand-edited on purpose - this is a policy, not a generated artifact.
//why: The design gate answered one question: may source be written yet? That left everything else ungoverned. Nothing stopped an agent writing production Terraform during REQUIREMENTS, or a deployment manifest before a single test existed. Both are code that outruns the decisions it depends on, which is the whole thing this layer exists to prevent.
//earliest: `earliest: X` means the phase BEFORE X must be cleared (APPROVED or INHERITED). So source needs DESIGN cleared - exactly the rule that already existed, generalised rather than replaced. A rule whose earliest is REQUIREMENTS has no prerequisite and never blocks.
//not-blind: This is deliberately narrow. Writing a test, a spec, a document or a memory-bank entry early is good practice, not a violation, so those are never blocked. Only artifacts that encode a decision from a later phase are gated.
//protected: The enforcement surface. An agent that can edit the hooks, their wiring, the policies they read or the records they produce can edit the rules it is being held to - and every one of these files was writable by the same Write tool the hooks govern. guard-write.mjs refuses the editor's Write/Edit/Delete on them; guard-bash.mjs refuses shell writes to them (redirects, Set-Content, rm, sed -i, node -e, git checkout -- ...). The list is unioned with the fallback in .claude/hooks/_lib.mjs, never replaced by it, so a project may protect more and never less. The single escape is CURSOR_PLATFORM_DEV=1 in the editor's environment, set by a human developing the platform itself; it is an environment variable and not a file because a file is something an agent can write.
//qualityConfig: The build gates. /postmortem's whole argument is that a finding becomes a BannedSymbols entry, an analyzer severity or a convention test rather than a document, and incidents.mjs check re-reads those files to prove the guard an incident bought is still there. All of which an agent could undo by editing one line of config - and a green build afterwards would say nothing was wrong. guard-write.mjs refuses an EDIT to one of these when it already exists; creating one is fine, because adding a gate is not weakening one. Escape for a human who has decided the rule itself is wrong: CLAUDE_ALLOW_QUALITY_CONFIG_EDIT=1.
//qualityConfig-vs-alwaysAllow: `.editorconfig` appears in both lists and that is not a conflict: they answer different questions. `alwaysAllow` is guard-phase's answer to WHEN a file may be written in the lifecycle - a build gate is never phase-gated, so it is always allowed. `qualityConfig` is guard-write's answer to WHO may edit one that already exists. Both hooks run on the same event and a refusal from either wins, so the narrower rule decides.
//qualityConfig-globs: Every entry starts with `**/` because globMatch's `*` does not span a separator: `.editorconfig` would match only at the repository root, and a solution-level one under backend/ would be unprotected.
//secretFiles: Files no agent may READ. This is the exact translation of the `Read(./x)` entries in .claude/settings.json permissions.deny, and self-audit A13 keeps the two equal. It is declared here rather than derived from settings.json at runtime because settings.json is Claude Code's alone: it does not exist in a Cursor-only checkout or in a plugin install, so a hook that read it would govern nothing on either - a control that exists and is unreachable, which is the defect self-audit was written to find. guard-read.mjs refuses these, with no escape variable: the value would land in the transcript, and the transcript is what the guard exists to keep it out of.

rules.why: Code written before the design gate implements a design nobody approved. This is the original rule and its behaviour is unchanged.
A migration is the physical schema made real. It follows docs/design/database-design.md; written before it, it becomes the design by default.
IaC encodes the deployment architecture, which is a phase 3 decision (/dotnet-iac-gen). Written during analysis it silently settles what the architecture review was supposed to decide.
A pipeline that builds and tests needs something to build and test. Generated by /deployment-pipeline-gen once the code exists.
Deploying is the last gate for a reason. A manifest written before the testing gate is a plan to ship something nobody has proven works.
